group.passage:
Understanding formal dining manners is simpler than it seems. By following a few basic guidelines, you can easily learn how to behave at a formal dinner.
One of the secrets is to understand the language of cutlery. Imagine your plate as a clock face. At the 9 o’clock position lies one or two forks for the main course, with the sharp side facing the center of the table. If there are two forks, the smaller one will be placed farther from the plate. To the right of the plate, spoons and knives are placed at the 3 o’clock position. On the outermost side lies the soup spoon, followed inwards by one or two knives. The knife should be positioned with the cutting blade facing the plate. If an appetizer or a salad is served, a salad fork, often the smallest, may appear at the 12 o’clock position.
If you need to have a short leave away from your table during a meal, you should place one fork and one knife on the sides of your plate with their tips facing each other in an upside-down V shape. Having finished the meal, you should place the knife and fork vertically in the center of the plate. However, if the tip of the knife is inserted between the teeth of the fork, it implies the food is below expectation. This is an indirect way to tell the staff that you are not satisfied with the quality of your meal.
Proper etiquette also involves napkin manners. When initially seated at the table, you should unfold the napkin and place it on your lap. Throughout the meal, keep the napkin on your lap. When needed, discreetly dab your mouth, not your face or hands, with the napkin. If you need to briefly leave the table, refold the napkin and place it to the right of your plate. Finally, after the last course, you should place the napkin loosely in the center of the table, not on the plate.

figures.label: 第1題選項 (A)–(D)
figures.caption: 第1題選項 (A)–(D)：四種餐具擺設圖
figures.description: 四個選項皆為黑白餐具剪影圖，排成 2×2（上排 (A)(B)、下排 (C)(D)）。每張圖中央是一個圓形餐盤（雙圈），餐盤左右兩側直立排放餐具，圖中沒有沙拉叉放在餐盤上方（12 點鐘方向）的情形，刀刃朝向無法從圖上清楚分辨。各選項由左至右的餐具依序為：(A) 小叉子、大叉子｜餐盤｜長刀、短刀、湯匙——叉子在左側且較小的叉子在外側，右側湯匙在最外側、刀子在內側；(B) 大叉子、小叉子｜餐盤｜湯匙、短刀、長刀——較小的叉子靠近餐盤，右側湯匙緊鄰餐盤、刀子在外側；(C) 湯匙、短刀、長刀｜餐盤｜大叉子、小叉子——湯匙和刀子在餐盤左側、叉子在餐盤右側（為 (A) 的左右鏡像）；(D) 湯匙、小叉子、大叉子｜餐盤｜長刀、短刀——湯匙放在左側叉子的外側，餐盤右側只有兩支刀子。
rows: 餐盤左側（由左至右，即由外而內）
餐盤右側（由左至右，即由內而外）

figures.label: this picture（第2題）
figures.caption: 第2題：餐盤上刀叉擺放的線條圖
figures.description: 題目右側一張黑白線條圖：一個圓形餐盤（雙圈），叉子從餐盤左下方斜向右上方擺放，刀子從餐盤右下方斜向左上方擺放，兩者在餐盤上方交叉，刀尖插入叉子的叉齒之間（不是倒 V 形分開擺在餐盤兩側，也不是上下直放在餐盤中央）。

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is the correct way to set the table?

options.A: ［圖］餐盤左側由外而內：較小的叉子、較大的叉子；餐盤右側由內而外：較長的刀子、較短的刀子、湯匙（湯匙在最外側）。
options.B: ［圖］餐盤左側由外而內：較大的叉子、較小的叉子；餐盤右側由內而外：湯匙、較短的刀子、較長的刀子（湯匙最靠近餐盤）。
options.C: ［圖］餐盤左側由外而內：湯匙、較短的刀子、較長的刀子；餐盤右側由內而外：較大的叉子、較小的叉子（叉子在餐盤右側）。
options.D: ［圖］餐盤左側由外而內：湯匙、較小的叉子、較大的叉子；餐盤右側由內而外：較長的刀子、較短的刀子（湯匙在餐盤左側）。

questions.stem: According to this passage, which of the following is true about napkins?

options.A: The napkin should be folded back again after the last course.

options.D: A napkin placed in the center of the table means the customer will be back soon.

options.D: Proper ways to position the cutlery after the last course.
